who: People in shared or quiet places
takeaways: If audio plays automatically for more than 3 seconds, people can pause or stop it, or turn its volume down separately from the system volume. Level A.
Screen reader users hear their reader through the same speakers. Autoplaying sound can drown it out, so they cannot even find the button to stop it.
Because it can make a whole page unusable, this rule applies to everything on the page, even parts that are not meant to conform.
The best fix is to not autoplay sound at all. If sound must play, keep it under 3 seconds, or put the pause or mute control at the very start of the page. Moving video is a separate rule, 2.2.2.
failures: A hero video that autoplays with sound
Background music with no pause or mute control
A mute button placed at the end of the page
check: List anything that makes sound without being asked: hero videos, ambient music, chat widgets, ads.
For each, check it is silent by default, stops within 3 seconds, or has a pause or volume control.
With a screen reader on, load the page and check you can hear the reader and reach the control quickly.

quiz.question: A brand campaign wants a hero video that plays with sound when the page loads. What is the best design?
options: Autoplay with sound, with a pause button in the footer
Autoplay with sound for 10 seconds, then fade out
Autoplay muted, with a clear unmute button on the video
quiz.why: Sound longer than 3 seconds needs a control, and a footer button is hard to reach while audio drowns out a screen reader. Starting muted avoids the problem. The moving video still needs a pause under 2.2.2.

spec: Mark every element that can make sound, and whether it autoplays.
Specify the default: muted, or the length of any sound that plays automatically.
Place pause and mute controls first in reading order, and name them clearly, such as “Pause background music”.
review: What makes noise on this page without anyone pressing play?
How would a screen reader user stop it while it talks over them?
Does the moving video also need a pause? That is 2.2.2.
tradeoff: Marketing wants instant impact, and sound grabs attention. Many browsers already block autoplay with sound, so start muted with a visible unmute control and let people choose.
system: Make video and audio components start muted when they autoplay, with pause and mute controls built in.
pitch: Sound nobody asked for drives people away, and for screen reader users it can make the page unusable. Start muted and let people turn it up.
